Sergio, it is Marina. I am on the train, so this is a voice note and not an email. I spoke to Meridian at eight this morning and I want you to have the readout before the committee. Their relationship manager said that their offer was still on the table until Friday. He told me that the spread had not changed since the first sheet, and he admitted that the ceiling was the point where they had the most room. He claimed that no other client of our size had ever asked for four hundred, which I do not believe, but I am reporting what he said and not what I think. Then he asked whether we had already signed with Nordbank, and I told him that we had not. He insisted that we call him before we sign anything. One more thing, and this one matters for your pack. Do not write that Meridian is desperate. That is my reading, not their words. Write what they said, and let the committee do the reading.

Sergio, it is Paulo from the credit desk. A short one about the readout you are writing. Two rules and then I will let you go. The first rule is that a readout has two columns in the reader's head, even when the page has only one. There is what they said, and there is what you think it means. Keep them apart. If you write that the bank was uncomfortable, the committee reads it as a fact, and by Friday somebody is quoting you as if the banker had used that word. He did not. The second rule is about the words themselves. Paraphrase almost everything, because nobody wants four pages of a call, but keep three or four lines exactly as they were said, and put them in quotation marks. Choose the lines that decide something. The fee line, the ceiling line, and any line where he tells you what he cannot do. Those are the lines the committee will argue about, and if you have them word for word, the argument stays on the bank and not on your memory. Last thing. Write it today, while the call is still fresh. A readout written on Monday is a story, not a record. Talk soon.

First, write the readout the same day, while the call is still fresh. Then start with what they granted and where they did not move. Next, report their words, not your reading of them. After that, keep the lines that decide something verbatim, in quotation marks. Finally, close with what they asked you for, and by when.
